name: Successful Layer Sets Force Empty Unique-Midpoint Core
statement: Every forbidden pc-minor produced by the complete common-seed occurrence-cover criterion has empty unique-midpoint core. More generally, any ample forbidden pc-minor with a successful layer set has empty core. Hence a nonempty unique-midpoint core excludes every successful layer set. The converse fails: an ample forbidden pc-minor may have empty core without admitting a successful layer set.
proof: The common-seed criterion makes every occurrence row corner-peelable. Each old-coordinate section is a proper pc-minor because the layer set is nonempty and the seed occurs in every layer, so every section is also corner-peelable. The layerwise core formula therefore gives an empty core. The terminal clause-recovery theorem places every successful layer presentation in this common-seed form. For the converse failure, the certified 292-concept obstruction has empty core and exactly one corner. Any successful layer presentation needs at least two nonempty proper rows to own opposite signed facets; each row has a corner that lifts to a distinct occurrence corner, contradicting uniqueness.
